pages.title: Smaller
pages.text: The last thing distortion taught me: size is a choice. Bent hard enough, a chamber folds and keeps working, small enough to stand on a pedestal.$(br2)Four of them around one heart, and the whole cycle runs in a single room.
The nexus needed more than a catalyst. A heart, grown around a nether star, from diamond, emerald, gold and netherite $(l:basics/compounds)compounds$().
When it beats, the four chambers fold into their cores. I choose a $(thing)target$(), feed it ores and water, and it does the rest.

pages.name: Alchemical Nexus
pages.text: Four cores on their pedestals around the nexus.

pages.title: One Machine
pages.text: When it wakes, each core tears a rift open and its chamber comes back through it, shrunk to a working miniature.$(br2)It breaks, changes, condenses and rebuilds on its own, and needs no molds.

pages.title: Its Habits
pages.text: Choosing a new target starts it over, though it keeps its fluids. Each stage eats what its own machine would, and the compounds between stages wait in a store of 256.$(br2)Any of the four cores opens it. And it still needs its $(l:energy/wormholes)wormhole$().
